The era of a single dominant AI platform is over.

Sensor Tower's State of AI Report, covered by TechCrunch on June 16, confirms that ChatGPT's market share has dropped below 50% for the first time. Google Gemini now commands 27.7%. Anthropic's Claude holds 10.3%.

For executives who built their AI strategy around a single provider, this is the inflection point that demands a reassessment. A fragmented market means vendor lock-in carries higher risk, switching costs are rising, and the feature gap between platforms is narrowing faster than procurement cycles can keep up.

This fragmentation will accelerate. Google is embedding Gemini across Android, Search, Home devices, and enterprise cloud simultaneously. Anthropic is carving out defensible positions in coding and safety-critical workflows. The competitive moat for any single AI platform is eroding quarter over quarter.

The strategic response is not to pick a winner. It is to architect for optionality — building AI capabilities on abstraction layers that let your organization leverage the best model for each use case without rewriting infrastructure every cycle.
